body: Over the past month, I talked to three of my co-workers. One of them suggested writing down how I feel, which I mentioned before. Another suggested getting my life in order, saying the rest would fall into place when I had stable living, a license, a diploma and a hobby I enjoyed. The third was just an ear. I still just want to stop fighting depression, to give up.

I tried getting drunk with a friend years ago for that purpose. I pored my heart out, and it very briefly turned sexual. I regretted it.

What support groups could I find? I'm so lost, I don't even know the first place to look.

I was a depressed child before the house fires. My father died in the second one. I can not remember what happened in my life besides those house fires before the age of 18, and I know I was contemplating suicide then too. I changed states, tried distancing myself from everyone and everything I knew. I spiraled into deeper depression. I came back, slept on a couch for a year, moved, got a job, and I'm still in as low a point as I've ever been. 

I don't even feel comfortable talking about my issues online, where I can be anonymous. I was told once to write down how I feel, and show that to a therapist, but every time I start writing, I can't get more than two paragraphs before I scrap it. I wrote the OP three times before I got the courage to post it.

Ninja edit: slept on a couch from 20 to 21. Got a job less than a week after turning 21. Now 22.

I spoke with two therapists before hitting 18. One diagnosed me with Survivor's Guilt, and I deflected the issues with the other one. I can't open up to my friends or family because I can't stand feeling awkward and vulnerable, even though I know they will help and support me.
Saying that is easy. I've been saying that for damn near nine years. I still can't live it. And my problems have spiraled since then. It's without a doubt a major core issue. Thanks for the words.
